title: Refit a gas burner after cleaning: turn the head until its slot drops round the igniter, then seat the cap
instruction: Put the burner head back on its base so it sits flat round the igniter, then put the cap on it, centred.
context: Anyone who cooks on gas lifts the burner heads and caps off to wipe up spills, then puts them back. The head only sits flat with its slot round the igniter; left riding on it, or with the cap off centre, the burner clicks, lights unevenly or burns yellow. Nothing locks: the head must go down already turned, by sight, and the cap nests on it.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Hob, fixed: front corner of a full-size gas hob, brushed steel deck 4.5 high, x 20 to 50, y -52 to 5.5; two black knobs (34 mm across, 20 mm tall) at x 22.5, y -10 and -17; a second, assembled burner at x 29, y -25.5. Front burner base, fixed, dark grey cast aluminium, axis x 29, y -1.5: flange 84 mm across, 4 mm thick (its top, 4.9 high, is the seat); spigot 52 mm across, 10 mm tall; white porcelain igniter 12 mm across, 16 mm above the seat, axis 36 mm from the burner axis toward +y. Burner head, loose, silver cast aluminium, 160 g: rim 75 mm across, 58 mm inside, 19 mm tall, with one 38 deg slot (5.7 mm each side of the igniter); crown over a 13 mm deep cavity (3 mm round and above the spigot); lip 56 mm across, 6 mm tall, on top. Burner cap, loose, black enamelled cast iron, 350 g: 76 mm across, 17 mm tall; its recess, 62 mm across and 8 mm deep, goes over the lip (3 mm per side) and its skirt rests on the rim. Drainer, fixed, pale blue plastic: tray 11 x 18, centre x 26, y 17.5, five ribs 0.6 wide along y, tops 3.5 high, at x 21.6 to 30.4. Head on the ribs at x 26, y 13, slot pointing 150 deg from +x; cap top up at x 26, y 22. Pan grate off.
scoring: From poses (top photo, ruler, straightedge); seat = flange top. Head seated: tilt under 2 deg, lowest point within 1.5 mm of the seat, axis within 3.5 mm of the burner axis, slot centre line within 12 deg of the igniter (igniter in the slot). Cap seated: right way up, tilt under 3 deg, axis within 4 mm of the burner axis, lowest point 18 to 21.5 mm above the seat (on the head's rim). Whole-run latch D: head or cap ever faster than 0.8 m/s (dropped about 3 cm or more, or thrown). The end score is 0 unless both grippers are 3 cm clear of both parts and both parts have been at rest (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s, neither more than 1 cm above every surface. Then 1.0: head and cap seated, no D. 0.5: head seated, cap not (on the drainer, on the lip, tilted, upside down), no D. 0.25: head seated with D. 0: anything else, including a head riding the igniter or off the base.
reset_notes: Lift the cap and head off, stand both back on the drainer at their marks, and turn the head so its slot points 150 deg from +x. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Full size and mass; round parts are 24-sided in collision. Gas, flame and spark are not simulated; the hob, base and second burner are fixed, the grate is off. Head and cap are rigid; the 18 flame ports are drawn, not cut. Friction 0.4 (0.3 enamel). The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a part still held, within 3 cm of a gripper, or over 1 cm above every surface scores 0. Pad contact with the igniter is not scored.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reached over the drainer and hob edge, left head and cap on the drainer); demo: 1.0 (left arm moved head then cap from drainer onto the burner, then retreated)
